title: Wander the Cult of Barnacle Bay - Let's Play and Review - Part 4
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-WID9zHoKhE

Tank and Ross surface at last. Daniel (@dungeondive) brings his **Wander: The Cult of Barnacle Bay** heroes up the ladder out of the flooded waterways and into Barnacle Bay proper, and the first thing he does is praise the tiles — flowerbeds, garden gates, shovels, woodpiles, a well, a town square. It isn't decorative art, he argues; it makes the place feel inhabited.

The scenario asks for three keys hidden among darkness tiles, then an exit — except the special rules imply a single key opens the magical gate while the objective demands all three. He flags the contradiction, can't resolve it, and asks viewers who've played it to weigh in. Setup itself makes him nervous, and he explains why with a scar: first-edition Mansions of Madness, where a setup error could render a scenario unwinnable and you'd never know until far too late.

Then the board fills. Four spawn cards deliver guards — shielded, line-of-sight-blocking, must-die-first tanks — plus brutes, casters and archers, and a hero hitting the next XP tier triggers yet another spawn. The dice are merciless. A rules point closes it out: his crit-counter can't strike a ranged attacker even at close range, per the designer. He disagrees thematically, plays it straight on camera, and says he'll house-rule it at home.

----

Daniel plays a rule he disagrees with on camera, then house-rules it privately. Where do you land when the designer's ruling breaks the fiction?
